sources.entry: CommaFeed - Google Reader inspired self-hosted RSS reader. (Demo, Source Code) Apache-2.0 Java/Docker

summary.one_liner: CommaFeed is a self-hosted, Google Reader-inspired RSS reader built on Quarkus and React/TypeScript.
summary.what_it_does: CommaFeed is a self-hosted RSS feed reader with a web interface offering four layouts, light and dark themes, and a responsive design for mobile and desktop. It supports keyboard shortcuts, right-to-left feeds, and OPML import/export. It exposes a REST API and implements the Fever and Google Reader APIs for native mobile apps. Users can define rules to automatically mark articles as read, and receive push notifications for new articles. It runs on an embedded H2 database by default or can be configured to use PostgreSQL, MySQL, or MariaDB.
use_cases: following news and blog feeds in one place
importing or exporting subscriptions via OPML
reading feeds in a native mobile app via Fever or Google Reader API
running a multi-user feed reader for a team or family
how_to_run: docker (see the Docker section of the README for image location)
Download a precompiled native or jvm package from the release page, then run it
npm install && npm run dev (frontend, in commafeed-client)
notable: Runs with zero configuration using an embedded H2 database
Compiles to native binaries for fast startup and low memory use
Implements both Fever and Google Reader APIs for mobile clients
Supports 25+ UI languages with a documented translation workflow
Includes detailed JVM memory tuning guidance for constrained systems
caveats: Native builds require GraalVM or a container runtime; building from source needs Maven and Node tooling for development
Local-network feeds are blocked by default to prevent SSRF and must be explicitly enabled
The public instance has limitations compared with self-hosted setups
